1.why: Text is a clean sans-serif with comfortable line and letter spacing, though it appears to be a standard system font rather than a purpose-built dyslexia typeface.

2.why: No italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs appear anywhere; all content is short sentence-case text.

3.why: The single-column layout with large type and full-width controls is readable and well organised at the mobile width shown.

4.why: Every instruction is a brief plain-language sentence, e.g. 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.'

5.why: Placeholders show the expected input format, such as 'name@example.com' and 'Example: 123456'.

6.why: No screen contains more than a few short sentences, so the user never reads a long block to proceed.

7.why: The verification code had to be typed by hand and no copy-to-clipboard option appears on any screen.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered anywhere in the observed flow.

9.why: Standard email and password fields would likely work with password managers, but the screenshots show no evidence of autocomplete or one-time-code autofill support for the OTP field.

10.why: The 'Step X of 4' banner and large blue buttons make position and action clear, though two solid buttons coexist after a code is sent.

11.why: Once a code is sent the screen shows two solid primary buttons ('Send code' and 'Check code') plus 'Send a new code', so more than one main action is presented at once.

12.why: Plain status banners follow each action, e.g. 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.'

13.why: The user can retry 'Check code' or 'Send a new code' after a mismatch without penalty and the entered code stays visible, though no reveal/hide toggle is provided.

14.why: The error 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.' states the problem and the fix without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown or expiry is visible and the banners explicitly say to enter the code 'when you are ready.'
